samples.description: Annual Compustat firm-year observations for 1979-1998 after current/prior value, SG&A<=sales, and positive-log screens; 109,388 source-screened rows include currency-status flags, 58 unlike-currency ratios are unavailable, and 107,562 unit-verified observations are retained after trimming for Model (I).

assumptions: Current local COMP.FUNDA xsga and sale are mapped to historical Compustat items #189 and #12 by matching catalog labels; vintage and item-number crosswalk remain unverified.
INDL, C, STD, and D approximate the described industrial-firm 1999 PST/full-coverage population; the source gives no SIC cutoff.
Trim using pooled 0.5th and 99.5th empirical percentile cutoffs for the dependent variable, log-sales change, and the interaction.
Exclude nonpositive values when needed to define logarithms.

If current and prior CURCD values match, compute the baseline ratios and decrease indicator in the same reported currency. If CURCD differs, leave those baseline variables unavailable because the provider guide, physical p. 71, does not establish the quote direction/arithmetic for CURRTR in this source; the observed rate pattern does not establish a safe multiply/divide rule.
Rows with a missing or different currency code retain the paper's source screens but have unavailable baseline variables and are excluded from estimation.
Use conventional homoskedastic OLS standard errors because the paper does not identify the Table 2 covariance procedure.
For two gvkey-fyear groups with distinct datadate values, retain the latest fiscal-year-end row; same-date duplicate keys stop construction.

limitations: Local Compustat coverage and population are current and are not confirmed to match the 1999 PST/full-coverage data.
The local xsga/sale mnemonics have matching labels, but the historical Compustat item-number crosswalk is not verified.
The exact industrial-firm screen and percentile tie handling are not fully reported.

The provider guide defines CURRTR as a balance-sheet-date exchange rate for translating foreign amounts to USD but does not state its arithmetic direction. Selected CURCD transitions have rates that do not establish a safe multiply/divide rule, so the unlike-currency constructions are left unavailable.
Table 2 does not identify the covariance procedure; conventional OLS standard errors are a documented best-effort assumption.

Current data produce 109,388 source-screened observations, 58 unlike-currency ratios unavailable, and 107,562 unit-verified observations after trimming, versus the paper’s 64,663 and 63,958; vintage/population differences remain unresolved and limit numerical comparability.
